name: Add Automatic Merge Conflict Resolution to the Git Plugin
description:
## Goal
Add an "Automatic Merge Conflict Resolution" section to the Git Plugin settings so Rowbly can automatically synchronize the current branch with its upstream branch, resolve conflicts in Rowbly data and configuration, and push the result without user intervention.

## Dependency
Blocked by ROW-13 (Allow disabling Automatic Commits while the Git Plugin is enabled). Complete ROW-13 before starting this Story. Keep this feature's enable/disable preference independent of Automatic Commits.

## Acceptance criteria
- Add an "Automatic Merge Conflict Resolution" section to the Git Plugin settings with an explicit enable/disable control.
- When enabled, support automatic runs on a configurable interval and an on-demand button in the Plugin settings. The interval must trigger runs automatically; it must not require pressing the button or confirming each run.
- Persist the enable/disable preference and interval. Clearly show whether the feature is enabled, the configured interval, whether a run is active, and the last run's result.
- Each run pulls the latest version of the current branch's configured upstream branch, merges that upstream branch into the current branch, automatically resolves all merge conflicts involving Rowbly data or configuration files, commits the completed merge when needed, and pushes the resulting current branch to its configured upstream.
- Resolve Rowbly data and configuration conflicts automatically using documented, deterministic rules that preserve valid records and configuration. Handle concurrent edits, additions, deletions, record-key collisions, and Plugin Data; validate the merged Data Root and perform any necessary automatic repairs before pushing. Never treat accepting one complete side and silently discarding the other side's changes as a general conflict-resolution strategy.
- Normal interval and on-demand runs, including Rowbly conflict resolution, must complete without prompts, an editor, manual conflict resolution, or approval before pushing. Define how automatic runs are scheduled and resumed across Rowbly restarts, and make the runtime requirements clear in the settings and documentation.
- Serialize synchronization runs and coordinate them with Rowbly writes and Automatic Commits so overlapping timers, button presses, or processes cannot corrupt data or Git state. Define how pending Rowbly changes are included when Automatic Commits are disabled.
- Do not automatically resolve conflicts outside Rowbly data or configuration, discard unrelated working-tree or staged changes, or force-push. If unrelated conflicts, missing upstream, authentication/network errors, or a rejected push prevent completion, stop safely, preserve local work, report the cause, and allow a subsequent automatic run to recover without leaving Rowbly unusable.
- Disabling the feature stops future scheduled runs and disables the on-demand action; document what happens to a run already in progress.
- Update the user guide, Git Plugin documentation, and the published Rowbly skill Git reference for the new settings, automatic scheduling, merge rules, push behavior, recovery, and interaction with Automatic Commits.

## Verification
Use two clones of a temporary remote to verify interval-triggered and button-triggered synchronization end to end: pull upstream changes, merge, automatically resolve concurrent Rowbly data/configuration changes, validate the Data Root, and push without intervention. Verify enable/disable and restart behavior, Automatic Commits both on and off, overlapping runs and writes, and safe recovery from unrelated conflicts, rejected pushes, and interrupted runs. Add deterministic regression coverage for data loss, corruption, and races in the existing test homes, following repository test policy.
